Mississippi State Department of Health boil-water notices and compliance records
City of Jackson water system public reporting
US DOJ and EPA Jackson water system case materials
Public reporting on 2022 O.B. Curtis Water Treatment Plant failure
_meta.note: Exploratory 12-phase N-D-C baseline for a dysfunctional municipal potable water system. Values are structured estimates for model demonstration and should be replaced with audited time-series data where available.

synthetic.label: AI structured baseline
synthetic.description: Generated from public Jackson water failure case materials for phase-map demonstration.

0.name: Source water and watershed condition
0.transformation: Surface-water source assigned to municipal treatment system

1.name: Raw water intake and pumping
1.transformation: Raw water moved from source into treatment intake

2.name: Coagulation, sedimentation, and filtration
2.transformation: Partially clarified water in treatment process

3.name: Disinfection and chemical treatment control
3.transformation: Chemically treated water intended to meet potable standards

4.name: Clearwell, storage, and finished-water pumping
4.transformation: Finished water held and pumped into distribution

5.name: Distribution network pressure
5.transformation: Pressurised potable water in pipe network

6.name: Household delivery and access
6.transformation: Water delivered to homes, businesses, and public facilities

7.name: Wastewater collection and conveyance
7.transformation: Used water collected into sewer system

9.name: Stormwater and flood stress interaction
9.transformation: Storm stress applied to potable, wastewater, and road-access systems

10.name: Regulatory monitoring and public notice
10.transformation: Compliance status and boil-water information communicated

11.name: Emergency water distribution and service restoration
11.transformation: Bottled-water logistics, repairs, and pressure restoration after failure

0.notes: Source water constraints are real but not the primary collapse point. Treatment and distribution failures dominate downstream risk.

1.notes: Raw water intake and pumping are vulnerable to equipment condition, power continuity, and flood/turbidity events.

2.notes: Treatment process reliability is a central bottleneck. Staffing gaps, chemical controls, sludge handling, and equipment condition reduce contribution capacity.

treatment_process_failure_flag.note: System-level treatment process reliability failure documented.

3.notes: Disinfection and treatment control degrade when operators, chemical feed, and process monitoring cannot meet safe-drinking-water constraints.

treatment_control_failure_flag.note: Chemical and operational control issues require time-series confirmation.

4.notes: Storage and finished-water pumping have limited public visibility. Storage cannot buffer the system when treatment and pressure failures coincide.

storage_resilience.note: Storage duration and operating margin not yet tabulated.

5.notes: Distribution pressure is the deepest physical failure mode. Pressure loss turns treated water into unreliable service and triggers contamination risk.

pressure_loss_failure.note: Loss of pressure and boil-water conditions documented.

6.notes: Household delivery fails when pressure, reliability, and public confidence fail. The material output is no longer reliably potable water at the tap.

boil_water_notice_exposure.note: Requires notice duration and affected population normalization.

7.notes: Wastewater collection remains part of the urban water cycle and can add fragility during storms, overflows, or infrastructure outages.

sewer_collection_condition.note: Needs sewer condition and overflow data.

8.notes: Wastewater treatment is adjacent to potable reliability because storm and sewer failures can compound public-health risk during water outages.

wastewater_permit_stress.note: Needs permit and discharge compliance time series.

9.notes: Stormwater and flood stress interacts with potable infrastructure during flooding and system disruptions. This is a cross-system fragility channel.

stormwater_interaction_risk.note: Needs event-based stormwater and wastewater incident data.

10.notes: Regulatory monitoring is comparatively transparent, but monitoring is a warning layer, not a physical repair layer.

regulatory_intervention_flag.note: Federal intervention and enforcement materials are public.

11.notes: Emergency water distribution and restoration become substitute infrastructure when the normal water chain fails. That protects households but confirms lifecycle degradation.

emergency_distribution_flag.note: Bottled-water distribution and emergency restoration publicly documented.

system.interpretation: Jackson is a chronic maintenance-collapse case. The water chain breaks at treatment control, distribution pressure, household delivery, storm stress, and emergency restoration. Regulatory monitoring is more visible than the physical system it is monitoring.
